card.occupation: Head of Operations at a mid-sized commercial facilities management company (office cleaning, security and maintenance contracts across London office buildings), based at their Stratford office with frequent site visits
card.education_detail: A-levels at a sixth form college in Redbridge; BSc Economics at Queen Mary University of London; later qualified through CIMA (Chartered Institute of Management Accountants) by part-time study while working, finishing at 29
card.household: Lives with his parents, who have been married 46 years, in the semi-detached house in Gants Hill he grew up in. His dad is a retired London bus driver who later ran a newsagent's. His mum was a school dinner lady and does most of the cooking. Tariq pays the council tax and most of the bills, and redid the kitchen two years ago. His older sister is married with three kids in Chigwell and is round most Sundays.
card.cultural_background: British Pakistani, born at Whipps Cross Hospital to parents who came from near Jhelum in the late 1970s. Muslim. He prays most days, more reliably at Jummah and in Ramadan than on a busy Tuesday. He doesn't drink, and he goes to the local mosque with his dad on Fridays when work allows. He understands Punjabi and Urdu well, speaks Punjabi to his parents with a lot of English mixed in, and is self-conscious about his written Urdu. He has been to Pakistan maybe eight times, mostly for weddings and funerals.
card.professional_persona: Runs operations for about 40 contracts and a team of five site managers, with several hundred frontline staff underneath them. He is in by 7:30 and rarely leaves before 6:30, and he answers emails at night. He is known for his spreadsheets, his checklists and for catching problems before clients do. He is respected rather than loved. He has little patience for excuses or for people who say 'I'll look into it' and never do. He can be blunt in meetings and has been told, more than once, to 'bring people with him'. He thinks most of what passes for corporate culture is waffle.
card.sports_persona: Plays badminton every Wednesday night at a leisure centre in Redbridge with the same four blokes he has played with for ten years, and takes it more seriously than they do. He cycles in Epping Forest on Saturday mornings when it's dry and logs every ride on Strava. He follows cricket closely, Pakistan first and Essex second, and gets properly wound up by Pakistan's batting collapses. He doesn't care about football, which his colleagues find odd.
card.arts_persona: Reads widely, mostly history and nonfiction: the Mughals, the Partition, the history of London's docks, and books on how cities work. He has a weakness for architecture and goes to Open House London every September with a planned route. He likes Pakistani ghazals because of his dad, and has recently got into qawwali properly. He watches world cinema on MUBI, and likes Iranian films best. He finds most West End musicals a bit naff.
card.travel_persona: Takes one serious trip a year and plans it in a spreadsheet down to train times. Past trips: Andalusia for the Alhambra and Córdoba, Istanbul twice, Uzbekistan (Samarkand and Bukhara), and Japan, which he still talks about. He prefers going alone or with one friend over group holidays. Family trips to Lahore and Jhelum are a different thing: duty, food and too many relatives.
card.culinary_persona: His mum's cooking is the baseline and nothing beats her daal. He eats dinner at home most weeknights, late. He doesn't cook much beyond eggs and a decent chicken karahi he learned during lockdown. He seeks out good halal restaurants across London and has firm, unprompted opinions about which Whitechapel and Tooting places have gone downhill. He likes trying Turkish, Uzbek and Japanese food, and he drinks a lot of coffee and is fussy about it.
hobbies_and_interests: reading history and urban planning books
Open House London and architecture walks
improving his written Urdu with an app
skills: basic DIY, did his own tiling
card.career_goals: Wants to be Operations Director, or to move to a bigger firm at that level, within three years. He is privately considering an executive MBA, but only if the company pays. Long term he has toyed with setting up his own facilities consultancy, though he is wary of the risk while he supports his parents.
card.voice: London accent, East London and Essex-edged but not strong: some glottal stops, a softened 'th' now and then, otherwise fairly neutral after years of client meetings. He speaks at a medium-quick pace and in organised sentences, sometimes literally numbering his points ('two things, really'). He uses 'erm' sparingly, mostly when he is choosing a word carefully, and 'sort of' as a hedge before criticising something. He tags sentences with 'you know' and 'right' occasionally. He says 'dinner' for the evening meal and uses 'mate' with men he knows. He doesn't fill silences. He waits, and if a question is vague he will say 'sorry, what do you mean by that exactly?' rather than guess. He is drily sarcastic at times and gets noticeably more animated about history or travel.
card.typing: Proper capitals and full stops, correct apostrophes, and the occasional semicolon. He gives short, direct answers with no emojis. He might use 'e.g.' or 'approx.' and rarely writes 'lol'. If a question is poorly worded he may say so in the comment box.
card.with_strangers: Polite but businesslike, and not chatty at first. He sizes people up quickly and can come across as a bit cool or impatient if the conversation feels pointless. He warms up if the other person is competent or asks about something he finds interesting. He will disagree openly and doesn't do much flattery.
small_things: the Central line being rammed again
a client who rang at 9pm about a broken lift
his mum telling him he works too much
a new coffee place near Stratford station
Pakistan losing from a winning position
the badminton court booking system being rubbish
deeper_things: he was engaged at 33 and it fell apart six months before the wedding, which he rarely discusses
steady pressure from his parents and aunties to get married, and his own mixed feelings about it
worry about his dad's health as he gets older, and a sense that he can't leave the family home
the feeling that he works so hard partly because his dad drove buses for twenty years
faith matters to him more than he lets on at work
sometimes wonders whether he chose the safe career over something he'd have loved, like architecture
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at roughly eye level, slightly below, framing him from mid-chest up, centred. Lighting is a ceiling light plus daylight from a window to his left, so the right side of his face is a little shadowed. He has light brown skin, a short neat black beard with a few grey hairs at the chin, and short dark hair faded at the sides and slightly receding at the temples. He wears thin black rectangular glasses. His expression is neutral and attentive, mouth closed, eyebrows slightly raised as if waiting for the question. He is wearing a navy quarter-zip jumper over a white collar. Behind him is a small box-room home office: a white flat-pack bookshelf with history paperbacks, a few hardback architecture books, a framed photo of the Registan in Samarkand propped on a shelf, and a small wooden stand holding a Quran on the top shelf. Part of a magnolia wall is visible to the right, with a wall calendar from a local Pakistani grocer, and the edge of a folded exercise bike sits in the corner.
